title: The Monkey and the Crocodile
place: A fruit tree beside the River Ganges
note: A new adaptation of Babbitt’s two-part “The Monkey and the Crocodile,” a Jātaka story associated with the Vānarinda Jātaka.

rights.basis: The 1912 source edition is identified as public domain in the United States by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: A monkey rides a crocodile across a broad river toward a fruit-covered island.

pageArt.alt: Midstream, Monkey calmly tells Crocodile that his heart was left hanging in the fruit tree.
Safe in the riverside fruit tree, Monkey speaks to Crocodile below about the trust he has lost.

scenes: Monkey lived in a fruit tree beside a wide river. Across the water grew an island laden with ripe mangoes.
Crocodile offered Monkey a ride to the island, but secretly planned to bring Monkey’s heart home for another crocodile to eat.
Halfway across, Crocodile revealed the plan. Monkey’s fear rose like the river, but he kept his voice calm.
“My heart?” Monkey said. “I never carry it when gathering fruit. I left it hanging in my tree. Turn back, and I will fetch it.”
Crocodile believed him and swam back. The instant they reached the bank, Monkey leapt into the highest branches.
“No creature leaves its heart behind,” Monkey called. “You tried to trick me, and now you have lost my trust.”
A calm mind had found a branch where strength could not reach.
